title: Non-Hermitian engineering of superfluidity in a Rashba spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas
authors: Pingcheng Zhu, Lihong Zhou, Jianxin Zhong
abstract: We investigate superfluid pairing in a two-dimensional Rashba spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas subject to spin-selective one-body loss. Within the non-Hermitian mean-field framework, we self- consistently solve the gap and number equations and find that moderate dissipation can significantly enhance the pairing gap, resulting in a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on the dissipation strength. Dissipation also provides an additional control parameter for driving the system across the BCS-BEC crossover. We further analyze the quasi-particle spectrum and identify two distinct superfluid regimes characterized by one and three exceptional rings, separated by an exceptional spectral transition. Interestingly, dissipation can enhance both pairing channels while simultaneously inducing a momentum-dependent phase twist in the triplet component. These results demonstrate that spin-selective dissipation provides a versatile non-Hermitian control knob for manipulating superfluid pairing, spectral structure, and crossover physics in spin-orbit-coupled quantum gases.
summary: This paper explores superfluidity in a spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas by introducing controlled dissipation. Using non-Hermitian mean-field theory, the authors demonstrate that moderate loss can unexpectedly enhance the pairing gap and allow continuous tuning across the BCS-BEC crossover. This establishes dissipation as a versatile control parameter for quantum gas physics.
main_problem: The study investigates how spin-selective dissipation (loss) affects superfluid pairing in a two-dimensional Fermi gas coupled with Rashba spin-orbit coupling.
main_result: Moderate dissipation significantly enhances the pairing gap in a non-monotonic fashion, providing a new control knob to tune the system across the BCS-BEC crossover and modify the spectral structure.
method: The authors employed a non-Hermitian mean-field BCS-BEC crossover theory, solving the gap and number equations self-consistently.
model_or_system: The system is a 2D Rashba spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas subjected to spin-dependent one-body loss ($\propto i\Gamma\sigma_z$). The theory uses the Bogoliubov-de Gennes formalism.
key_observables: Pairing gap ($\Delta_0$), chemical potential ($\mu$), quasiparticle spectrum (exceptional rings), and singlet/triplet pairing correlations.
important_parameters: Dissipation strength ($\Gamma$), SOC strength ($\alpha$), and interaction strength ($E_b$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the non-Hermitian mean-field approximation and assumes a symmetric solution for the order parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-monotonic dependence of $\Delta_0$ and $\mu$ on $\Gamma$ and $\alpha$, the reconstruction of the Density of States (DOS) in the complex plane, and the phase diagram showing 1ER vs. 3ER superfluid regimes.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, solving the self-consistent gap and number equations, analyzing the resulting quasiparticle spectrum (exceptional rings), and finally discussing the implications for pairing enhancement and crossover physics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends standard BCS/BEC theory into the non-Hermitian domain, showing how engineered dissipation can actively enhance quantum correlations, a key topic in open quantum systems.
